data.name: Izfaar
data.gender_notes: Izfaar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'afar', meaning 'to ride' or 'to journey'. In Islamic history, Izfaar refers to those who travel in the way of Allah, seeking knowledge or spreading the message of Islam. The name Izfaar carries the meaning “Rider, Traveler” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Izfaar usually hope their child will grow to embody rider, traveler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a journey of faith and spiritual growth, reminding us to remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.
data.etymology: Izfaar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rider, Traveler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Izfaar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: إزفار
in_arabic.meaning: إزفار يعني التغيير أو التحول إلى الأفضل
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم إزفار مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ز-ف-ر' والذي يعني التغيير أو التحول. وقد ورد في بعض التفاسير أن اسم إزفار يدل على تغيير الحال إلى الأفضل أو التحول إلى مرحلة جديدة أكثر إيجابية. كما يوحي الاسم بقدرة صاحبه على التكيف والتغيير للأفضل.

in_urdu.name: ازفار
in_urdu.meaning: ازفار کا مطلب تبدیلی یا بہتری کی طرف جانا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ازفار نام عربی جڑ 'ز-ف-ر' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے تبدیلی یا بہتری. یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں ایک نئی شروعات یا بہتری کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے. جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے درمیان، یہ نام امید اور مستقبل کی بہتری کی علامت کے طور پر استعمال ہوتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: इज़फार
in_hindi.meaning: इज़फार का अर्थ है परिवर्तन या सुधार की ओर जाना
in_hindi.long_meaning: इज़फार नाम अरबी मूल 'ز-ف-ر' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है परिवर्तन या सुधार. यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में एक नए आरंभ या सकारात्मक परिवर्तन के प्रतीक के रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है. यह नाम अपने धारक की सकारात्मक बदलाव लाने की क्षमता को दर्शाता है.

in_pashto.name: إزفار
in_pashto.meaning: إزفار د بدلون یا ښه والي معنی ورکوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: د إزفار نوم د عربيې ريښې 'ز-ف-ر' څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې د بدلون یا ښه والي معنی ورکوي. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، دا نوم د نوي پيل یا ښه راتلونکي اشاره کوي. دا نوم د خپل خاوند د بدلون او پرمختګ د توان په معنا دی.

The idea of setting out on a journey for learning or religious purposes reflects the spiritual and intellectual courage of early Muslims who put aside their personal interests to contribute to the broader Muslim community. This difficult yet noble pursuit has been celebrated in Islamic literature, poetry, and art, and continues to inspire countless individuals to embark on similar journeys today.

Traveling in the way of Allah grants us the opportunity to create a positive impact on society by spreading the message of peace, love, and compassion. This ultimately helps us develop a strong relationship with Allah and strengthens our faith, as we strive to follow His command through servicing others and seeking knowledge.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah' (1377 AD) The name Izfaar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun mentions 'Izfaar' as an example of a military term, specifically a banner carried by the Berber warriors of the Marinids. The term 'Izfaar' is described as a 'white flag with a green palm tree'.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'The History of the Prophets and Kings' (1403 AD) The name Izfaar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi recounts the story of the Ayyubid Sultan Al-Malik Al-Nasir and his military commander, Melek al-Kamel. During their campaign against the Crusaders, Al-Nasir is said to have gifted Melek al-Kamel a banner called 'Izfaar' as a symbol of his favor and esteem.
